## Re-baseline against the Windows tree (2026-11-16)

On 2026-11-16 the Windows working tree (source of truth, read-only) had UNCOMMITTED changes made after this map was written (HEAD was still `dceb47d`). That working tree was the truth from then on; the baseline snapshot is `git diff HEAD` sha256 `f5c0376d32bc37ee1f6e4914016372c123c558c9e539261cee3ad066c6c8e56d` (18 changed paths: 2 docs, 6 production .py, 7 test files, 1 new untracked test helper, 2 QA json). No `cpp_extensions` file changed (the native boolean rule is untouched). All Windows tests pass: the six changed non-threejs test files 26 passed (10 subtests), the Three.js renderer test file 36 passed, the regression ring 280 passed (244 subtests), 0 failed; 17 new tests and 3 updated writer tests.

**Update 2026-11-18.** Windows committed this work as `6d4786f` (parent `dceb47d`), and its tree is clean at that commit. The commit changes the same 18 paths (2 docs, 6 production .py, 7 test files, 1 new test helper, 2 QA json). The Windows line citations of the six production files and of `AGENTS.md` given in the table below were re-read at `6d4786f` and still hold (`boolean_operations.py` 26-34 and 42; `base_exporter.py` 78-79, 163 and 214-215; `dxf_exporter.py` 30; `fbx_exporter.py` 29; `obj_exporter.py` 76; `mesh_factory.py` 1, 14, 91, 94-111 and 161; `AGENTS.md` 502-516). Byte-identity of the commit with the earlier snapshot was not established (only the same 18 paths and these citations were checked), and the snapshot hash below was not reproduced (the uncommitted tree no longer exists); it stays as the record of what was mapped. The iOS side of this rule is done: one shared Core boolean pass (`Core/Meshing/BooleanPass.*`, `Core/Meshing/ExportMeshSet.*`) is called by `Services/ProjectService.mm` and `Services/ExportService.mm` (items MSH-16, RB-01, RB-02, RB-03, RB-04, EXP-05, EXP-22, MSH-15, MSH-19b: all `fixed`).

**Update 2026-11-20.** Windows committed one more change, `b9902e6` (parent `6d4786f`). It has its own section, [Re-baseline 2026-11-20](#rebaseline-2026-11-20); the tables of this section keep the state of 2026-11-16 / 2026-11-18 and cite Windows lines of `dceb47d` / `6d4786f` (history).

**Update 2026-11-21.** Windows committed two more changes, `bf6b8fc` and `49a2d59` (job 6). They have their own section, [Re-baseline 2026-11-21](#rebaseline-2026-11-21); the tables of this section still keep the state of 2026-11-16 / 2026-11-18 (history).

What changed on Windows: one export rule for the 3D view, HTML, OBJ, DXF and FBX (a negative cuts only positives of the same `condition_type`, a fully consumed positive is dropped, `condition_type` is mandatory in the boolean pass), the writers read only the post-boolean mesh and never rebuild, an export with no surviving mesh fails before writing anything, and a wall whose drop-stub union fails keeps the plain wall and logs one warning with the takeoff UID.

Outcome for the decision items: the Windows author resolved MSH-16 (option b: one rule everywhere), EXP-22 (option b: one unified rule, reported as an Export Error) and MSH-19b (option b: keep the plain wall) in the Windows tree; the user then chose to follow the fixed behavior (section E). MSH-19 is `no-longer-divergent` (iOS applies `remove_degenerate_faces` to the union since commit 42ad10d). EXP-M02 and EXP-19 remained open questions after the re-baseline and are decided in section E (keep outward normals; adopt the colour-management and lighting constants only). Stale rows of the feature table (section G) and the FBX line of section H were corrected in this pass.

**bf6b8fc** (39 files, 5933 insertions, 2223 deletions: 19 production files, 16 test files, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the two quality ledgers; 49 new Windows test methods, none removed). ## Method

1. Twelve area mappers read the iOS code and the Windows code and tests, and executed both sides wherever the behaviour was numeric: the real iOS C++ sources were compiled on the host with MSVC (plus the vendored sqlite3.c and pugixml) and compared with the Windows Python modules and native `.pyd` extensions run with `python -B` and `-p no:cacheprovider`. Obj-C/UIKit code could not be compiled in that environment (no Xcode); those items are established by reading both sides and re-implementing the arithmetic. The first successful GitHub Actions runs (2026-11-20 UTC) later compiled every Obj-C and Obj-C++ file of the code of `5dc7b2b` and `787a57d` against the real iPhoneOS 18.5 SDK, and a third run (44678523124) built the code up to `275cf66` the same way; a fourth run (44856186199, 2026-11-21 UTC) built the code of job 5 up to `df456a2` the same way; a fifth run (44953904172, 2026-11-21 UTC) built the code of job 6 up to `e151655` the same way (compiled and linked, nothing run; see What was and was not verified).
2. Twelve independent verifiers re-checked every mapper divergence (re-running the numbers), corrected citations and test plans, and added missed items.
3. This synthesis merged mapper and verifier per area: CONFIRMED items are kept with the verifier corrections; AMBIGUOUS items become `needs-decision`; CANNOT_REPRODUCE items become `cannot-reproduce`; REFUTED items are dropped and counted; verifier "missed" items are added as CONFIRMED. All 12 verifiers returned results, so no item is flagged `unverified`.
4. Cross-area duplicates (the same underlying difference reported by several areas) were merged: one id is kept (its original mapper id), the other ids are listed as aliases and their test plans are kept under `aliasTestPlans` in the JSON. A merged item takes the highest impact of its members. Each kept item has ONE owner area for the fix phase (the area whose primary iOS file it lives in); when the primary file is shared, the owner is the area that owns the logic being changed.
5. Ranking: impact class first (wrong-numbers, data-safety, behavior, ui-cosmetic), then by how many users and flows are affected and how central the code is (explicit order for the big classes, then number of reporting areas), then fix before needs-decision.

Impact classes: **wrong-numbers** = a number, measurement, coordinate, exported value or stored value differs from Windows; **data-safety** = data can be lost, corrupted, overwritten or left inconsistent; **behavior** = observable logic/ordering/validation/flow differs; **ui-cosmetic** = presentation only.

Disposition: `fix` = Windows behaviour is clear and reproducible, or the user decided to port it, and the item was ported (see the final status); `wont-fix` = closed by a user decision (the item block and section E give the reason); `needs-decision` = iOS behaviour was kept and the question is listed for the user (the 8 items that were `blocked-needs-decision` until 2026-11-19; the user decided them that day and they were `wont-fix`; since job 5 (2026-11-20) four of them (BRW-09, EXP-13, IMP-20, RPV-29) are still `wont-fix`, EXP-12 and LP-24 are `fixed` and DBP-04 and EXP-16 are `no-longer-divergent`; the Phase 1 disposition `fix` is shown next to it); `cannot-reproduce` = cannot be reproduced on iOS (section F); `no-longer-divergent` = the difference disappeared (iOS already fixed or Windows changed; MSH-19, and since job 5 DBP-04, EXP-16 and LP-22, where Windows converged on the iOS behaviour). Testability: `core-cpp` = host unit test against Core with the Config/Tests/ harness; `needs-extraction-from-objc` = logic had to be moved from .mm into Core first; `objc-only` = UIKit/manual or device test. Verdict: result of the independent verifier (`REBASELINE` for RB-* items). Status (final, 2026-11-21, job 8; job 6 of 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-20 before; first set 2026-11-18): `fixed` = ported and covered by host unit tests and/or the Obj-C syntax check (since job 8 four of these, COND-ELEV-01, COND-STYLE-02, DLG-FINITE-01 and COND-M08, are also verified on device: DEV-01 to DEV-11 all PASS on the owner's iPhone); `fixed-ui-unverified` = ported, but part of the behaviour is Obj-C/UIKit/Metal/WebKit that was syntax-checked against hand-written stubs (the code up to `275cf66` also compiled against the real iPhoneOS SDK without errors in the CI runs of 2026-11-20 UTC (runs 44654559214, 44661853681 and 44678523124), the Obj-C(++) changes of job 5 compile too (run 44856186199 of 2026-11-21 UTC, head `df456a2`, success), so do those of job 6 (run 44953904172 of 2026-11-21 UTC, head `e151655`, success), and nothing of it had run on a device or simulator before job 8; the device checks DEV-01 to DEV-11 of job 8 passed on the owner's iPhone) and, for the items that remain fixed-ui-unverified (23 since job 8), needs a device or simulator check (the outcome line names it); `blocked-needs-decision` = not ported under the standing rule, iOS behaviour kept and the question listed for the user (no item has this status since 2026-11-19: the user decided the 8 items, see section E); `wont-fix`, `cannot-reproduce` and `no-longer-divergent` as above. The status each item had before the final pass (`open`, `decided`, `closed`) is `statusBefore` in the JSON; the status before the decisions of 2026-11-19 is `statusBeforeDecision`.

How to read an item block: the `Windows:` line and the `iOS (as mapped):` line describe the two sides when the map was made (the iOS side is the code BEFORE the fix, so it often describes what no longer exists); the last line, `outcome (...)`, says what was done, in which files, and what could not be verified. Phase 1 `note`, `rebaselined`, `decision`, `fix scope` and `closed` lines are kept as history. Since job 5 (2026-11-20) a record that `b9902e6` or the job-5 code changes also carries `Superseded / updated 2026-11-20 (job 5)` lines, its `outcome` is rewritten where it contradicted the code or Windows `b9902e6`, and its former `possible Windows defect` line is now a condensed `Windows defect record` with the resolution (the original text is in `possibleWindowsDefect` of the JSON record); the `Windows:` and `iOS (as mapped):` lines stay the Phase 1 description (Windows `dceb47d` / `6d4786f` numbering). Verification wording in the outcome lines (for example "only syntax-checked against stubs") is as of 2026-11-18/19 and is not rewritten item by item: the Obj-C and Obj-C++ files up to `275cf66` also compiled against the real iPhoneOS SDK in the successful CI runs (2026-11-20 UTC; runs 44654559214, 44661853681 and 44678523124) and those of job 5 in run 44856186199 (2026-11-21 UTC, head `df456a2`) and those of job 6 in run 44953904172 (2026-11-21 UTC, head `e151655`), which still says nothing about behaviour on a device or simulator. Since job 6 (2026-11-21) a record that `49a2d59` or the job-6 code changes carries `Superseded / updated 2026-11-21 (job 6)` lines in the same way (COND-M08, COND-ELEV-01, DLG-FINITE-01, COND-STYLE-02, COND-DUP-01, IMP-20); the Windows `file:line` values written in job 6 are those of `49a2d59`. Since job 8 (2026-11-21) the nine records that the device checks DEV-01 to DEV-11 cover by item id (COND-ELEV-01, COND-STYLE-02, DLG-FINITE-01, COND-M08, COND-PLACE-01, LP-24, LP-22, EXP-12, EXP-16) end with a `device check (2026-11-21, job 8)` line; the outcome and "Unverified" / "Not verified" wording above it is the state before job 8.

Feature status in section G is as reported by the mapper: `matches`, `diverges`, `unverified`, `platform-adapted`.

**Host unit tests (`Config/Tests`).** The tests live in `Config/Tests`, not in a top-level `Tests/`, because Nyxian compiles every `.cpp` outside the top-level `Config/` and `Resources/` folders. They are one CMake project; GitHub Actions runs `cmake -S Config/Tests -B build/tests -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`, `cmake --build build/tests --parallel "$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"` (bounded to the runner's core count since commit 787a57d; a bare `--parallel` is an unlimited `make -j` that made the host-test step take 55 min 20 s instead of 168 s) and `ctest --test-dir build/tests --output-on-failure --no-tests=error`. Before the fix phase the repo had **0 iOS behaviour tests** (only the 10 self-tests of the harness, area Harness); on 2026-11-19 there were 1588 behaviour tests plus those 10 (22 of them were added on 2026-11-19 for the four code changes: Conditions +16, Settings +6). **Obj-C syntax check.** The platform-layer `.mm` and `.m` files (27 files) were checked with `zig clang -x objective-c++ -fsyntax-only` against HAND-WRITTEN stub Foundation, UIKit, QuartzCore and CoreGraphics headers: **27 of 27 files ok, 0 errors, 4 warnings** (re-run on 2026-11-19 after the four code changes: same result; the 4 warnings are baseline protocol/category warnings about the `UITableViewDataSource` methods of the condition editor, not new; re-run on 2026-11-20 after the Obj-C(++) changes of job 5: 27 of 27 files, 0 errors, the same 4 warnings; re-run on 2026-11-21 after the Obj-C(++) changes of job 6: 27 of 27 files, 0 errors, the same 4 warnings). This catches typos, wrong Core call signatures and missing includes. It does NOT validate against the real Apple SDK, ARC or runtime behaviour, UIKit layout and gestures, Metal shaders or any UI behaviour. The checker and the stubs are scratch tooling kept outside the repo. The compile against the real Apple SDK that followed on CI (for the code up to `787a57d`, again up to `275cf66`, for job 5 up to `df456a2` and for job 6 up to `e151655`) is described in the next paragraph.

The workflow `Build IPA` (`.github/workflows/build.yml`, job `build-ipa`, runner image macos-15-arm64, Xcode 16.4 (16F6), iPhoneOS 18.5 SDK, Apple clang 17.0.0) has since run every step on the code of the commits 5dc7b2b and 787a57d: runs 44654559214 (commit 5dc7b2b) and 44661853681 (commit 787a57d) succeeded. A fourth run, 44856186199 (event push of branch ios-parity-sync, head commit df456a2, created 2026-11-21 02:29:37 UTC, finished 02:32:50 UTC), succeeded on the first try and covered the four commits of job 5 (d07abe1, 31dd319, 37fb424, df456a2; its results are at the end of this paragraph). Two earlier runs failed in the host unit tests and never reached the later steps: 43782525569 (2026-11-16, commit 42b46c3, a fused multiply-add difference in a curved-mesh oracle, fixed by `Core/Geometry/strict_fp.hpp`) and 44642251350 (commit 292c406, `MarkerAnchor.CountTriangleAndCurvedBand` of RPV-27; the cause is inferred, see below). ## (A) Wrong numbers

66 items, global rank order. All former `needs-decision` items are decided (section E); `cannot-reproduce` items are in section F; `wont-fix` and `no-longer-divergent` items stay listed with their reason. Each block ends with its final `outcome` (status, what was done, files); the `Windows:` and `iOS (as mapped):` lines describe the two sides when the map was made, so the iOS side is the code before the fix.

#### 1. MSH-01: iOS divides all mesh coordinates and dimensions by the page scale ratio; Windows meshes in raw OST units
- owner: meshing | impact: wrong-numbers | disposition: fix | testable: needs-extraction-from-objc | verdict: CONFIRMED | status: fixed
- aliases: GEO-01, LP-01, EXP-04
- Windows: `infrastructure/visualization_provider.py:114,131-139; meshing/mesh_builder.py:106; exporters/base_exporter.py:26; renderers/threejs/mesh_processor.py:45; ...`: transform_to_3d(x,y) = (-(x/1.0), y/1.0) and ost_to_real_units(v) = v/1.0 for every page. The page sf2/sf1 never scales vertices, heights, thickness or offsets; it is only used for the page size in the flip/rotate transform. 3D coordinates are therefore OST (real-world) units for all pages.
- iOS (as mapped): `Services/ProjectService.mm:119,170; Services/ExportService.mm:30,57 (sr = 1.0 / project.page_scale_ratio(page_uid), Core/Data/ProjectData.hpp:30-38) feeding Core/Meshing/ ...`: Every coordinate, height, thickness, width, depth and z offset is multiplied by 1/(sf2/sf1) of the takeoff's page. Model is paper-scale, different pages get different scales, and absolute tolerances (boolean kSnapTol 0.05, h_len < 0.001, arc radius tolerance 0.1, segment counts chord/5) act at a different relative size.
- Windows tests: tests/integration/rendering/test_page_flip_mesh.py::test_mesh_pipeline_preserves_model_scale_when_flipping; tests/integration/rendering/test_page_flip_mesh.py::PageFlip3DMeshTests::test_mesh_pipeline_preserves_model_scale_when_flipping; tests/domain/services/test_coordinate_transformation_service.py::OSTCoordinateSystemThreeDTests
- note (Phase 1): Earlier iOS log claims this matches desktop transform_to_3d(..., scale_ratio); it does not match the current Windows pipeline (see staleDocClaims). Fixing this also removes the sr = inf risk for sf2 = 0. Fix first: MSH-02 depends on it. Call sites: ProjectService.mm, ExportService.mm (sr = 1/ratio).
- outcome (fixed): ProjectService.generateMeshesIntoRenderer and ExportService use generate_view_meshes / generate_*_export: raw OST units, no division by the page scale ratio (the local Phase 1 loops and build_hole_map are deleted). Files: `Core/Meshing/TakeoffMeshBuilder.hpp, Core/Meshing/TakeoffMeshBuilder.cpp, Core/Meshing/MeshFactory.hpp, Services/ProjectService.mm, Services/ExportService.mm`.

#### 2. QTY-01: Takeoffs with a parent_uid are skipped for every condition type (attachments placed on areas count 0)
- owner: quantities | impact: wrong-numbers | disposition: fix | testable: core-cpp | verdict: CONFIRMED | status: fixed
- aliases: COND-M01, LP-05
- Windows: `ost_visualizer/domain/services/condition_quantity_service.py:85-91`: primaries = takeoffs where (not condition.is_area) or parent_uid is root ('', '0', 'None'). Only AREA takeoffs with a parent are treated as holes. Non-area conditions count every takeoff even when parent_uid is set, so an attachment placed on an area contributes its own quantity (count 1).
- iOS (as mapped): `Core/Domain/UomService.hpp:767-768`: 'if (t->is_hole()) continue;' is applied for every condition type, so Attachment (and any non-area) takeoffs that have a parent are dropped. Imported attachments therefore report 0. Verified: lifecycle fixture gives attachment q1=0 (Windows 1) and linear [5,7] with a parent gives 5 (Windows 12).
- Windows tests: tests/domain/services/test_condition_quantity_service.py::TakeoffLifecycleQuantityTests::test_attachment_contributes_its_own_quantity; tests/domain/services/test_condition_quantity_service.py::ConditionQuantityServiceExactTests::test_non_area_conditions_count_every_takeoff_even_with_a_parent_uid; tests/domain/services/test_condition_quantity_service.py (parent/hole cases) (+2 more, see PARITY_DIVERGENCES.json)
- note (Phase 1): Same is_hole skip exists in ProjectService.mm:167 for mesh generation (mesh area, unverified). LP-05 is the umbrella for compute_page_quantities: it also covers QTY-02, QTY-03, QTY-04 and QTY-18. COND-M01 is the same defect seen from the conditions list.
- outcome (fixed): compute_page_quantities skips a takeoff as a hole only when its condition is an AREA condition (cdn.is_area() && t->is_hole()); linear/count/attachment takeoffs with a parent_uid are counted (attachment on an area = 1, linear [5,7] with parent = 12). Parent token 'None' (QTY-18, needs-decision) deliberately left on the 2-token Takeoff::is_hole rule and not tested. Files: `Core/Domain/UomService.hpp`.

#### 5. QTY-10: Area slope factor must use absolute rise and run (iOS uses signed values)
- owner: quantities | impact: wrong-numbers | disposition: fix | testable: core-cpp | verdict: CONFIRMED | status: fixed
- aliases: COND-AREAABS-01
- Windows: `ost_visualizer/domain/services/uom_service.py:676-682,731-735`: _calc_slope_factor(rise, run, use_absolute=(condition_type == AREA)): for areas abs(rise), abs(run) are used. Linear: only strictly positive rise AND run give sqrt(rise²+run²)/run; negative values are not a slope.
- iOS (as mapped): `Core/Domain/UomService.hpp:518-523,673`: Always signed: for Area, a negative rise or run gives factor 1.0. Verified: 120x120 area, rise=-3, run=4, calc 11, SF -> 100.0 (Windows 125.0); also affects perimeter calc 14/15/33, calc 17, 21, 22, 34 and 35 and the hole area/perimeter scaling.
- Windows tests: tests/domain/services/test_uom_service.py::AreaSlopeBehaviorTests::test_area_quantity_uses_absolute_slope_magnitude; tests/domain/services/test_uom_service.py::UomGeometryHelperTests::test_slope_factor_is_the_hypotenuse_over_run_and_ignores_flat_or_unset_slopes; tests/domain/services/test_uom_service.py::UomAreaQuantityTests::test_slope_scales_area_perimeter_and_hole_measures_and_uses_magnitudes (+5 more, see PARITY_DIVERGENCES.json)
- note (Phase 1): The dialog-side half (store abs() for Area rise/run) is DLG-RISE-01.
- outcome (fixed): calc_slope_factor(rise, run, use_absolute=false); calculate_condition_quantities passes use_absolute for Area so negative rise/run use their magnitudes (120x120, rise -3, run 4 -> 125 SF); Linear stays strictly-positive only. Dialog half (store abs() for Area rise/run) is DLG-RISE-01, not part of this item. Files: `Core/Domain/UomService.hpp`.

#### 6. QTY-06: UOM normalization by measurement system (bid.measure_base) and calc-type compatibility is missing
- owner: quantities | impact: wrong-numbers | disposition: fix | testable: core-cpp | verdict: CONFIRMED | status: fixed
- aliases: COND-UOMNORM-01, DBP-06, UNITS-M01
- Windows: `ost_visualizer/domain/services/uom_service.py:246-312; loaded at ost_visualizer/infrastructure/mdb/components/bid_data_reader.py:1005; project_data_service.py:275,327`: On every condition load (and when conditions are replaced) normalize_condition_uoms_for_system(condition, metric = bid.measure_base == 1) rewrites uom1-3: imperial->metric {1,2,3->13; 4,5,6,7->14; 8,9->16}, metric->imperial {11,13->2; 12,14->5; 15,16->8}, others unchanged; ...

Files: `Core/Import/CabExtractor.hpp, Core/Import/CabExtractor.cpp, Services/ImportService.mm`.

Windows reloads the conditions after every save, so this matches its effective behavior; the 2026-11-19 'possible Windows defect' (the dialog accepted elevation text that the loader reads differently or not at all) was fixed by Windows b9902e6, and the 'deviation' is plain parity since job 5 (see below). THE RULE: after the shared parser accepts the text, the dialog refuses it when ALL of these hold: there is no ASCII `"` (U+0022) anywhere in it; a foot mark (U+0027 or U+2032) is followed, with or without Unicode white space, by one ASCII letter or digit [0-9A-Za-z]; and the rest is not a lone `x` / `X` (white space is allowed after it; decided for each foot mark). Refused (imperial and metric bid): `5'6`, `5'6x`, `10'6`, `5'abc`, `-2'3`, `5<U+2032>6`; accepted: `5'x` (60), `5'X` (60), `-4'x` (-48), `5' 6"` and `5'6"` (66), `10'6 1/2"` (126.5). The LOADER and the Core parser are UNCHANGED: a stored name such as "Footing @T 5'6" still reads 60 inches, top (pinned), and `10'6` still reads 120 in the loader. The statement of the job-5 line above that Windows "accepts `5'6` ... as 60 inches" is history for `5'6`: owner note a of job 5 ("report `5'6` -> 60 in to Windows") is RESOLVED, Windows fixed it in `49a2d59` (`5'x` is still accepted as 60 by design). iOS CHANGED: NEW `ost_domain::elevation_text_needs_closing_inch_mark` (Core/Domain/ConditionFormRules.hpp:87, ConditionFormRules.cpp:69), called by `parse_elevation_z` (ConditionFormRules.cpp:46, the call at :61-62) after `elevation_text_inches`, with the same title and message and the hint of the bid; no Obj-C change (`EditConditionViewController.mm:612` already shows the issue). Tests: NEW file `Config/Tests/Conditions/test_condition_elevation_foot_mark.cpp`, suite `CondElev02_ClosingInchMark`, 14 tests (one table of 189 rows computed with the real Windows `elevation_text_inches` and the regex run in memory, each row in an imperial and a metric bid with the Top / Bottom reload check, and the rule on the free function): TextRightAfterTheFootMarkNeedsAClosingInchMark, FeetWithXAndFeetWithClosedInchesAreStillAccepted, TheLoaderStillReadsAStoredFeetDigitNameAsFeet, TheRefusalIsTheExistingMessageWithTheHintOfTheBid, TheRuleOnTheFreeFunction, WhiteSpaceAfterTheXIsStrippedButOtherCharactersAreNot, OnlyAsciiLettersAndDigitsCountAfterTheFootMark, OnlyTheAsciiDoubleQuoteSwitchesTheRuleOff, EveryFootMarkOfTheTextIsChecked, ThePrimeMarkBehavesLikeTheApostrophe, TextsWithoutAFootMarkAndTextsTheSharedParserRefusesAreUnchanged, TheXFamilyAndTheDecimalAndZeroRowsOfTheOracle, ForeignMarksAndMarksWithoutReadableFeetStayRefused, TheEdgesOfTheAsciiClassAndAnUpperCaseLetterAfterTheMark. Changed tests (names unchanged): `CondElev01_Validation.AnAcceptedElevationReloadsToTheValueTheDialogSaved` (the row `5'6` is removed, the checked count 44 -> 40; `5'x` stays) and `CondElev01_Elevation.TheTextGivesZAndNanIsRefused` (`10'6` is refused now, `10'6"` gives 126.0 as before); comment-only edits in test_condition_elevation.cpp (of its 261 names the dialog accepts 90, it was 93; the loader values and every assertion are unchanged) and Parsers/test_elevation_text_value.cpp (the shared parser still gives `5'6` = 60). Method: red first (8 of the 12 tests of the first form of the new file failed, every failing check being a "must be refused" check, no acceptance check failed), then green; 26 mutants of the rule (M01 to M26), 25 killed (one of them, the class without upper case letters, survived the first 13 tests and was killed by the 14th) and 1 equivalent (the rule fed the unstripped text, shown equal on 579,195 short texts); the reviewers compared a line-by-line Python translation of the C++ foot-mark loop (not the C++ itself) with the verbatim Windows regex on all 14,900,788 strings of length 0-5 over a 27-character alphabet plus 3,000,000 random strings (0 differences) and all 189 table rows against the real Windows functions (0 mismatches; the host test runs the rows through the compiled C++); the independent mutation re-check of the final tree (three testers, 100 mutants in all) ran 41 mutants of the rule: 37 killed and 4 equivalent, none survived (`PORTING_LOG.md`, entry of job 6). Consequence for existing data (parity, owner-visible): a condition whose stored name ends in a feet-digit suffix such as "Footing @T 5'6" opens with `5'6` in the Elevation field, and every dirty save of that condition is refused until the elevation is fixed or cleared (iOS validates only when the form is dirty: EditConditionViewController.mm:359-363; Windows `_apply_changes` validates only a dirty form too: edit_condition_dialog.py:1760-1765; read, not run). With any negative mesh in the export the untouched positives come out with the opposite sign (-57600, -60000).

- outcome (wont-fix): Cylinders and curved walls are outward-facing (positive volume) and wired. Every exported mesh stays outward-facing, with or without a negative. DECIDED 2026-11-19 (keep iOS, no code change; alias MSH-M02 follows; same line as EXP-M02 / GEO-15 / EXP-17). (History, `6d4786f`: Windows core/boolean_operations.py:49-61 + adapters/obj_writer.py:38-43 flipped every positive when any negative existed and swapped faces again, so one OBJ mixed both windings; for `b9902e6` see Superseded / updated 2026-11-20 (job 5) below.) Pinned by ObjWinding.BooleanDifferenceResultsAreOutwardFacing (renamed 2026-11-20 from BooleanResultsStayOutwardFacingWithANegativeInTheExport), BooleanRule.Winding_ThePassNeverReversesTheFacesOfAPositive and ExportRule.Winding_EveryMeshThatLeavesTheViewAndBothExportsIsOutwardFacing. Files: `Core/Meshing/gen_count.cpp, Core/Meshing/gen_curved.cpp`.
- decision (2026-11-19): keep iOS: Every exported OBJ mesh stays outward-facing, with or without a negative of another type in the export. No code change. Covers the alias MSH-M02 (same line as the decided EXP-M02 / GEO-15 / EXP-17). Pinned by: ObjWinding.BooleanDifferenceResultsAreOutwardFacing (renamed 2026-11-20 from BooleanResultsStayOutwardFacingWithANegativeInTheExport); ObjWinding.ExportedMeshesHaveThePositiveSignedVolumeOfTheWindowsObj; ObjWinding.EveryCurvedWallAndCylinderVariantIsOutwardFacing.
- Updated 2026-11-20 (job 5): the decision stands and iOS has no code change, but Windows changed differently from what the 2026-11-19 suggested fix said (flip only entries flagged `boolean_applied`). Windows `b9902e6` (`boolean_operations.py:37-111`): `_bounds_overlap` is a strict `<` test on the bounding boxes (touching counts as apart), `_positives_with_cut_flags` (:51-67) marks a positive as "may be cut" when its bounding box overlaps a same-type negative's (an empty positive counts as may-be-cut, an empty negative is ignored), and `apply_boolean_operations` (:70-111) returns the ORIGINAL mesh, with its generator winding, for a positive that may not be cut (:96-98) and flips (f0, f2, f1) only the native result of one that may be (:99); `boolean_union` still always flips (:121). So an untouched positive no longer turns inside-out when a negative of another type exists, and the per-shape winding split of EXP-17 remains (pinned by Windows' own integration test `test_uncut_winding_with_negatives.py`: OBJ volume rhombus -1150, wall +800). The statements "flips EVERY positive when any negative exists" and "one OBJ mixes both windings because of the flip" above are history of `6d4786f`. Windows tests: `test_boolean_operations.py` `UncutPositiveWindingTests` (:124, 4 tests), the integration test above. iOS keeps EVERY mesh outward (decided: GEO-15, EXP-13, EXP-M02, EXP-17, MSH-21); nothing in iOS consumes or inverts the old flip (checked by reading: `BooleanPass` never touches faces, the shaders flip the normal towards the viewer and no back-face culling is used, the OBJ writer writes faces as stored, the Three.js viewer lights with screen-space derivatives). The bounding-box pre-check is NOT ported: only the vertex / face-list identity and the speed of an uncut same-type positive differ (iOS rebuilds it through the difference; the exact effect on a box is inferred, never run). Pinned by BooleanRule.Winding_ThePassNeverReversesTheFacesOfAPositive (test_boolean_rule.cpp:164), ExportRule.Winding_EveryMeshThatLeavesTheViewAndBothExportsIsOutwardFacing (test_export_mesh_set.cpp:642) with its Manifold twin ExportRuleManifold.Winding_EveryMeshThatLeavesTheViewAndBothExportsIsOutwardFacingWithManifold (:650), and ObjWinding.BooleanDifferenceResultsAreOutwardFacing (test_obj_writer.cpp:599; renamed from BooleanResultsStayOutwardFacingWithANegativeInTheExport, which only called boolean_difference_batch). Status stays wont-fix.
- possible Windows defect (CHANGED DIFFERENTLY on Windows by `b9902e6`, not the way the 2026-11-19 finding suggested; severity inconsistent, confidence medium): at `6d4786f` `boolean_operations.py:10-12` and `:49-61` flipped every mesh the native call returned although the native code returns two different windings (a mesh that went through the boolean comes out outward, an untouched positive comes out in the generators' inward convention), so one OBJ mixed windings and a negative of another type turned untouched positives inside-out (native code: `cpp_extensions/src/module_geometry.cpp:58-71`, `:95-103`, `boolean/boolean_ops.cpp:225-229`, `:781-788`; `obj_writer.py:38-43`). `b9902e6` replaced the blanket flip by the bounding-box rule (`boolean_operations.py:37-111`, see the Updated line above): untouched positives keep the generator winding and are no longer turned inside-out by a negative of another type. What stays inconsistent on Windows is the generators' own winding (EXP-17, unchanged), so an OBJ can still hold both windings. The wording "possible Windows defect" stays for that remainder.

#### 122. EXP-12: Name sanitisation rules differ (OBJ group/material and DXF layer)
- owner: export-formats | impact: behavior | disposition: fix (Phase 1: fix; was needs-decision until 2026-11-19, wont-fix 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-20) | testable: core-cpp | verdict: CONFIRMED | status: fixed
- Windows: `ost_visualizer/presentation/visualization/exporters/base_exporter.py:175-201 (_sanitize_material_name; was 172-198)`: Replaces ' ' '/' '\\' ':' ';' '*' '?' '<' '>' '|' '.' '(' ')' '[' ']' '{' '}' with '_', and removes '"' "'" ','. All other characters are kept (non-ASCII, #, &, =, %, +, -, @). A leading digit gets the 'Mat_' prefix. An empty result becomes 'Unknown'.
- iOS (as mapped): `Core/Export/obj_writer.cpp:84-102`: Whitelist: keeps ASCII alnum, '_' and '-'; ' ' becomes '_'; every other byte is dropped (all UTF-8 non-ASCII bytes vanish); no digit prefix; empty becomes 'mesh'. DXF layer names are not sanitised at all (ExportService.mm:144).
- Windows tests: tests/presentation/visualization/exporters/test_obj_exporter.py
- note (Phase 1, superseded where it conflicts with the re-baseline): Apply the Windows sanitiser to DXF layer names too. DXF forbids <>/\":;?*|=` in layer names.
- rebaselined 2026-11-16 (disposition stays fix): base_exporter.py line shift (+3 after line 163).
- outcome (fixed): Sanitisation rule and DXF layer name = OBJ material name are wired and tested. Since job 5 (2026-11-20) every control character U+0000-U+001F and U+007F of a condition name becomes ONE `_` in the exported OBJ group / material names and the DXF layer names, like Windows `b9902e6` (`base_exporter.py:15` `_CONTROL_CHARACTERS`, :200 `.translate(_CONTROL_CHARACTERS)` inside `_sanitize_material_name` :177-204): only these 33 characters; U+0085, U+2028, U+2029 and U+00A0 are untouched. Core/Export/export_text.cpp `sanitize_material_name` (:165) replaces each control byte with one `_` in the same pass, so the digit-prefix and the empty-name rules see the final text (a name that starts with a line break and then `1x` becomes `_1x`, before `Mat_1x`; a name that is only a line break becomes `_`, before `Unknown`). Superseded / updated 2026-11-20 (job 5): the 2026-11-19 decision "drop control characters, keep iOS" (the `decision` line below, history) is replaced by the user's instruction of job 5 to follow the fixed Windows behaviour; the "possible Windows defect" of that decision (Windows kept the characters) was fixed on Windows. Tests: ExportText.Exp12_ControlCharactersBecomeUnderscoresLikeWindows, Exp12_InjectedLinesCannotSurviveInAMaterialName, Exp12_PrintableAndNonAsciiTextIsUnchangedByTheControlCharacterRule, Exp12_TheDigitRuleAndTheEmptyRuleSeeTheReplacedText (Config/Tests/Export/test_export_text.cpp:37-87); ObjWriter.Exp12_ControlCharactersInANameBecomeUnderscoresInGUsemtlAndNewmtl, ObjWriter.Exp12_EveryControlCharacterOfANameIsOneUnderscoreInTheFile (test_obj_writer.cpp:282, :314); ExportGroups.Exp12_ControlCharactersOfAConditionNameBecomeUnderscoresInTheMaterialName, ExportGroups.Exp12_ALineBreakOrNulInAConditionNameInjectsNoLineIntoTheObjMtlOrDxf (test_export_mesh_set.cpp:1018, :1035; the second covers the DXF layer path, which no Windows test covers). Removed: ExportText.SanitizeMaterialNameDropsControlCharactersUnlikeWindows (its cases live on in Exp12_TheDigitRuleAndTheEmptyRuleSeeTheReplacedText with the new values). The oracle table kSanitizeCases (ExportTextOracleData.hpp) has 569 rows, none with a control character; re-verified unchanged against `b9902e6` (0 rows differ). HTML (json_string) and file names are untouched. Files: `Core/Export/export_text.cpp, Core/Export/export_text.hpp, Core/Export/UnicodeDigitData.hpp, Core/Export/obj_writer.cpp, Core/Export/obj_writer.hpp, Services/ExportService.mm, Config/Tests/Export/test_export_text.cpp, Config/Tests/Export/test_obj_writer.cpp, Config/Tests/Export/test_export_mesh_set.cpp`.
- decision (2026-11-19; superseded 2026-11-20 (job 5), see below): keep iOS: Control characters (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F) are dropped from exported OBJ group / material names and DXF layer names; Windows keeps them. No code change. Pinned by: ExportText.SanitizeMaterialNameDropsControlCharactersUnlikeWindows (removed 2026-11-20, replaced by the Exp12_ tests); ObjWriter.GroupAndMaterialNamesAreSanitisedLikeWindows.
- Superseded / updated 2026-11-20 (job 5): Windows `b9902e6` fixed it: `base_exporter.py:15` `_CONTROL_CHARACTERS = {code: "_" for code in (*range(0x20), 0x7F)}` and :200 `.translate(_CONTROL_CHARACTERS)`; the scope is exactly U+0000-U+001F and U+007F (the Unicode line separators U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029, which the 2026-11-19 suggested fix listed, are not replaced), the digit rule (:202-203) and the `Unknown` rule (:204) run after it. Windows tests: `test_base_exporter.py:123-138` `MaterialNameControlCharacterTests` (3 tests). The 2026-11-19 premise "Windows keeps the control characters" is therefore false. iOS CHANGED (not a "keep" any more): control bytes become one `_` each (see the outcome above); status wont-fix -> fixed, disposition wont-fix -> fix.
- Windows defect record (FIXED on Windows by `b9902e6`, 2026-11-19; was "possible Windows defect", severity unsafe, confidence high): at `6d4786f` `_sanitize_material_name` (`base_exporter.py:175-201`) kept CR, LF, TAB, NUL and other control characters, so a condition name with a line break corrupted or injected statements into the OBJ, MTL and DXF (and made the DXF layer table invalid). Fixed in `b9902e6` at `base_exporter.py:15` and `:200` (see above). The other locations of the finding (`obj_exporter.py` comment lines, `dxf_exporter.py:21-22`, `edit_condition_dialog.py:1410`) are covered by the same change or unchanged; the comment lines are EXP-16.

Obj-C: ViewController+Layers.mm single toggle and Show All / Hide All call _suspendPlacementForLayerHide (before the layers change, via _leavePlacement, remembering the tool revision) and _restorePlacementAfterLayerShow (last, via _selectConditionForPlacement:Enter) and reload the Conditions list ([condVC loadConditionsFromProject:] + reselect) so the greyed rows follow. Status check (final runs of 2026-11-19): host tests 1598 pass (MSVC), Conditions 174 pass on the clang+fma build, Obj-C syntax check 27/27 files 0 errors (4 baseline warnings). The list reload only matters while the Conditions sheet is alive (conditionsVC is weak; reopening it always loads fresh). - Superseded / updated 2026-11-20 (job 5): the two open notes are closed (see the two `open question` lines below): note 1 (the Image-layer exemption of the single toggle, with the tap guard and the floating-button refusal) is implemented like Windows, note 2 is no longer a defect. - open question (CLOSED 2026-11-20, job 5: PORTED): note 1: Image-layer exemption on hide. Windows has the exemption for the SINGLE-layer toggle only: `ui_event_coordinator.py:6474-6477` (`image_layer = self.project_data.is_image_layer_uid(layer_uid)`; `if not show and not image_layer: self._suspend_active_layer_tool(layer_uid)`) and :6504-6505 (`if show and not image_layer: self._restore_suspended_layer_tool(layer_uid)`), so hiding the Image layer does not suspend a placement and showing it does not restore one; Hide All and Show All (:6728-6729, :6752-6753) stay unguarded. A tap for the then hidden condition is ignored (`placement_mode.py:1648`, in `handle_place_press` :1639; entering is refused by `enter_place_mode_for_condition`, :1865, check :1869). It was an iOS divergence, not a Windows defect (the 2026-11-19 wording "judged an edge case, not a Windows defect; copy the exemption?" and "iOS treats the Image layer like any other layer" is history). iOS now: `ost_domain::is_image_layer_uid` (Core/Domain/Layer.hpp:54, LayerMerge.cpp:80) and a defaulted flag on `suspended_placement_for_layer_hide` and `restore_of_suspended_placement` (Core/Domain/ConditionChoices.hpp:145 and :187; :115 and :157 until job 6); ViewController+Layers.mm computes the flag once for the single toggle and passes NO for Hide All / Show All; hiding the Image layer with the single toggle does not suspend a placement (also not for a condition on that layer), showing it does not touch an existing suspension. Companion guard that Windows has: `ost_data::placement_tap_accepted(project, condition_uid)` (Core/Data/ProjectData.hpp:143) is true only when the condition exists and is visible; it is used by the placement sink (ViewController.mm:1310-1318, the last line of defence for tap, drag and polygon), by the floating mode button (ViewController.mm:741-764: a refused Place calls `_leavePlacement`, which clears the armed condition and switches Place off in the ring) and by a new optional delegate query `planView:canPlaceWithCondition:` (PlanView.h:29, PlanView+Placement.mm:264) that PlanView asks at the start of a tap and of a pan (no preview, no polygon point, nothing, like Windows). The old overload `ost_domain::placement_tap_accepted(bool)` is gone. Tests (Config/Tests/Persistence/test_placement_image_layer.cpp): CondPlace01_ImageLayer.HidingTheImageLayerDoesNotSuspendEvenForAConditionOnIt (:123), CondPlace01_ImageLayer.ShowingTheImageLayerKeepsAnExistingSuspension (:145), CondPlace01_ImageLayer.HideAllStillSuspendsAConditionOnTheImageLayerAndShowAllRestoresIt (:180), CondPlace01_ImageLayerUid.IsImageLayerUid (:215), CondPlace01_TapGuard.* (4: :253, :284, :305, :329). The Obj-C wiring (sink, floating button, delegate query, ViewController+Layers.mm) is syntax-checked against stubs and compiles against the real SDK (GitHub run 44856186199, success) but has never run on a device; status stays fixed-ui-unverified.
- open question (CLOSED 2026-11-20, job 5: NO LONGER A DEFECT): note 2: layer-less conditions on Hide All. Hide All with an armed placement of a layer-less condition: since Windows `b9902e6` Hide All no longer marks layer-less conditions hidden (`project_data_service.py:675-700`, the LP-22 fix), so the tool stays armed on a visible, placeable condition; the snapshot never suspends it (`ui_event_coordinator.py:1474-1491`, pinned by `test_ui_event_coordinator.py:18908-18912`). iOS: a layer-less condition is never suspended (`suspended_placement_for_layer_hide`) and stays visible after Hide All (LP-22: no-longer-divergent). Nothing to port. #### 172. QTY-19: Takeoffs with fewer than 2 position values are dropped at load, so count/attachment quantities can differ
- owner: database-persistence | impact: behavior | disposition: fix | testable: core-cpp | verdict: CONFIRMED | status: fixed
- aliases: POS-M02
- Windows: `ost_visualizer/infrastructure/mdb/components/bid_data_reader.py:1116-1200 (position at 1124/1167); parse_position at domain/utils/position.py:5-18`: Every takeoff row is kept (empty or unparsable Position gives []). Count/attachment calc 23 still counts 1 for such a takeoff; linear/area give 0. A takeoff pointing at a missing condition aborts the load with an integrity error instead of being dropped.
- iOS (as mapped): `Core/Persistence/ProjectStore/Components/ProjectStore+Load.cpp:264-267`: push_back only when the condition exists and position.size()>=2. parse_position returns {} on any unparsable token, so such takeoffs vanish and do not count. Missing-condition takeoffs are skipped silently.
- Windows tests: tests/domain/services/test_condition_quantity_service.py::ChildKindAndRoundingBoundaryTests::test_a_takeoff_without_geometry_totals_zero
- note (Phase 1): Likely a deliberate defensive filter; only the product owner can say whether a position-less count should show. Overlaps the persistence area.
- decision 2026-11-16: option (a) Keep them with an empty position (counts match Windows; PlanView and mesh code must tolerate empty positions). User: "keep takeoffs with empty positions (counts must match Windows). PlanView and mesh code must tolerate empty positions"

#### 177. BRW-M01: Folder (project) display order is locale-aware/case-insensitive on Windows but SQLite BINARY / std::string < on iOS
- owner: project-browser | impact: behavior | disposition: fix | testable: core-cpp | verdict: CONFIRMED (verifier-added) | status: fixed
- Windows: `ost_visualizer/presentation/components/project_tree_view.py:453-454 (sortByColumn(0, Ascending)) and :641-655 (_create_project_item builds a plain QTreeWidgetItem); ...`: Project nodes are plain QTreeWidgetItem, so the tree orders them with Qt's default item compare, which is locale-aware and case-insensitive at primary level (lowercase before uppercase on ties). Measured with PySide6 6.10.1 / Qt 6.10.1, locale en_US, offscreen, a plain QTreeWidget sorted ascending on column 0. ...
- iOS (as mapped): `Core/Persistence/ProjectStore/Components/ProjectStore+Folders.cpp:29-31 (ORDER BY Name, SQLite BINARY, no UID tie-break); ...`: Binary byte order, so every uppercase name sorts before every lowercase name ('Zebra' before 'apple'). The mapper judged the folder ordering as 'matches (same as Qt)'. That was wrong for mixed-case, accented and punctuation names. The Windows tests only pin Alpha/Beta/Alpha, which hides the difference.
- Windows tests: tests/infrastructure/mdb/components/test_hierarchy_reader.py::test_full_hierarchy_maps_every_bid_field_and_orders_bids_and_projects (reader order only; no Windows test pins the Qt collation)
- note (Phase 1): Evidence is an empirical Qt run (the scripts were scratch files outside both repos and are not kept). The exact order is locale-dependent, so the user must decide how close to match. It also affects the page-selector folder order (BRW-17).
- decision 2026-11-16: option (a) Case-insensitive ASCII compare with tie-breaks (fold, then lowercase first, then UID). User: "case-insensitive ASCII compare, then lowercase first, then UID"
- fix scope (set by the decision, owner project-browser): Folder display order: case-insensitive ASCII compare, then lowercase first, then UID.
- outcome (fixed): Decided (a): folder display order = case-insensitive ASCII compare (only A-Z fold, other bytes unsigned), then lowercase first at the first differing byte, then UID ascending numerically. Implemented as ost_domain::compare_folder_names / compare_folder_uids / folder_precedes (header-only, reusable) and applied in load_hierarchy (SQL ORDER BY Name, UID + stable sort). Item pl... Files: `Core/Domain/DatabaseHierarchy.hpp, Core/Persistence/ProjectStore/Components/ProjectStore+Folders.cpp`.

#### 178. CAM-04: Pinch zoom clamp is a fixed 1..500 that the fit distance can exceed; Windows clamps relative to the scene
- owner: settings-undo-camera | impact: behavior | disposition: fix | testable: needs-extraction-from-objc | verdict: CONFIRMED | status: fixed
- Windows: `cpp_extensions/src/renderer/renderer.cpp:291-315 (Camera::zoom, configure_clip_planes)`: new_distance = clamp(distance - delta*distance*0.001, 2*near, 0.5*far), where near = max(0.1, 0.001*size) and far = max(10000, 20*size), so the limits scale with the scene. Native results from distance 100: zoom(+120) gives 88.0; zoom(-120) gives 112.0; zoom(+1e6) gives 0.2; zoom(-1e9) gives 5000.0.
- iOS (as mapped): `Controllers/ViewController/Components/CameraController.mm:108-121; Rendering/Renderer.mm:474-477`: cameraDistance is clamped to [1.0, 500.0] on every pinch change, while fitCameraToMeshes sets distance = 2.5*maxExtent with no upper bound. For maxExtent > 200 the first pinch event, even with zero delta, snaps the camera inward to 500.
- Windows tests: tests/integration/native/test_renderer_boundaries.py
- note (Phase 1): iOS near and far planes are computed per frame, so the clamp must be redefined together with them; the unit scale of the iOS scene was not verified here. Pinch rate (delta*dist*0.5) is platform-adapted.
- decision 2026-11-16: option (a) Scene-relative clamp using the Windows limits expressed in iOS scene units. User: "scene-relative zoom clamp with the Windows limits in iOS scene units"
- fix scope (set by the decision, owner settings-undo-camera): Scene-relative pinch-zoom clamp using the Windows limits expressed in iOS scene units (the fit distance can no longer exceed the clamp).
- outcome (fixed): Both wiring entries done: Renderer gets the read-only property sceneMaxExtent (largest side of the union of the mesh bounds, 0 without meshes; independent of _sceneRadius) and CameraController _handlePinch uses camera_clip_planes_for_extent(sceneMaxExtent) (default_camera_clip_planes() without meshes) and zoom_camera_distance(distance, delta, kPinchZoomRate, planes); the fix... Files: `Core/Domain/CameraLimits.hpp, Rendering/Renderer.h, Rendering/Renderer.mm, Controllers/ViewController/Components/CameraController.mm`.

Nothing in iOS depends on it; iOS keeps every mesh outward. The possible Windows defect below is unchanged in `b9902e6` and stays recorded.
- possible Windows defect (unchanged in `b9902e6`, kept): ost_visualizer/presentation/visualization/exporters/adapters/obj_writer.py:38-43; ost_visualizer/presentation/visualization/utils/mesh.py:29-45; ost_visualizer/presentation/visualization/utils/mesh.py:268-275; ost_visualizer/presentation/visualization/utils/mesh.py:299-303; ost_visualizer/presentation/visualization/utils/mesh.py:332-343; ost_visualizer/presentation/visualization/meshing/mesh_factory.py:229-236; tests/presentation/visualization/utils/test_mesh.py:234-241; tests/presentation/visualization/exporters/adapters/test_obj_writer.py:10: The OBJ writer applies the same face swap to every mesh, but the generators wind differently: boxes, radial prisms and areas are inward, triangle and rhombus prisms outward. So even with no negative in the export, the triangle and rhombus count shapes come out inside-out in the OBJ while every other shape is outward. The unused mesh_type argument of _transform_faces suggests per-type handling was intended. Vertex order and triangulation differences are not defects. The Windows test docstring itself records the table disagreement and that no sign contract exists. Scenario: A bid with a triangle-shaped count condition next to walls: in the exported OBJ the triangle prisms are inside-out (negative volume) and are culled or shaded wrongly by viewers that use back-face culling, while all other shapes look right. Severity: inconsistent, confidence: medium. Suggested Windows fix: Make the generator tables consistent (reverse get_triangle_mesh_faces and get_rhombus_mesh_faces so they wind like the box and radial tables) or make _transform_faces use its mesh_type, and add a signed-volume test per shape. (Unchanged in `b9902e6`, checked 2026-11-20: `obj_writer.py:38-43` and the generator tables are not among the changed files; Windows now pins the split with `test_uncut_winding_with_negatives.py`.)

#### 205. RPV-27: Negative marker anchor is the vertex mean; Windows uses the area-weighted path centroid
- owner: rendering-planview | impact: ui-cosmetic | disposition: fix | testable: needs-extraction-from-objc | verdict: CONFIRMED | status: fixed
- Windows: `takeoff_renderer.py:390-437, 464-483`: Marker centre = polygon area centroid of the item path (MoveTo/LineTo points), falling back to the nearest interior anchor when the centroid is outside the shape, or the vertex mean for zero area.
- iOS (as mapped): `PlanView/PlanView.mm:346-355`: Arithmetic mean of the transformed vertices (for count shapes, the position point).
- Windows tests: tests/presentation/visualization/pdf/renderers/test_takeoff_renderer.py::test_area_with_hole_uses_anchor_inside_visible_fill; ::test_the_marker_is_drawn_over_a_negative_takeoff
- note (Phase 1): Linear and symmetric count shapes agree.
- outcome (fixed): The negative marker sits at Windows' _path_centroid of the takeoff path: Core negative_marker_anchor / canvas_marker_anchor = area-weighted centroid of the path points (closeSubpath repeats the start point, so a zero-area path gives the mean WITH that point), else, when Qt's QPainterPath.contains says the centroid is outside, the nearest interior point (vertex fractions then... Area with backouts: Windows uses the point order of Qt QPathClipper (not reproducible); iOS uses the region centroid with the Windows contract (anchor inside the visible fill). DECIDED 2026-11-19 (keep, no code change): (a) the area-weighted-centroid anchor of the region with a nearest-interior fallback and (b) the marker at the centroid of the displayed shape on rotated or flipped pages both stay. Windows defect for (b) FIXED on Windows by `b9902e6` (takeoff_renderer.py:385-416: the marker is an anchor item with the two marker rectangles as child items, so the page transform of zoom_handler.py:339-348 / :362-379 moves the anchor and the rectangles follow the shape; the 6d4786f citations :105-116 and :390-417 are history); iOS already matched and is pinned by MarkerAnchor.FollowsTheDisplayedShapeOnEveryRotationAndFlip (Config/Tests/Geometry/test_takeoff_footprint.cpp:805). Files: `PlanView/PlanView.mm, PlanView/PlanView.h, PlanView/PlanView_Internal.h, Core/Geometry/takeoff_footprint.hpp, Core/Geometry/takeoff_footprint.cpp`.
- decision (2026-11-19; part (b) superseded 2026-11-20 (job 5), see below): keep iOS: (a) The negative marker anchor (area-weighted centroid of the region with a nearest-interior fallback) stays; (b) the marker position at the centroid of the displayed shape on rotated or flipped pages stays. No code change. Pinned by: MarkerAnchor.MatchesPathCentroidOfTheWindowsRenderer; MarkerAnchor.AnchorOfAnAreaWithAHoleIsInsideTheVisibleFill; MarkerAnchor.CountTriangleAndCurvedBand; MarkerAnchor.PolygonAreaCentroid. CI note (2026-11-20 UTC): on arm64 (AppleClang 17) MarkerAnchor.CountTriangleAndCurvedBand failed once (x 77.4244 against 72.5756): on a mirror-symmetric curved band the two best grid centres of the marker-anchor search are mirror images whose squared distances tie bit for bit on the x86-64 builds (MSVC, clang), so the first wins, as in Windows; the arm64 run picked the mirror one. The cause, a last-bit libm difference in the atan2/cos/sin arc points, is inferred and was not observed on arm64. The assertion now accepts the Windows x or its mirror (150 - x), and a libm-free test, MarkerAnchor.AnExactTieKeepsTheFirstCandidateOfTheWindowsOrder, pins the tie rule; no app code changed. On a device the marker of an exactly mirror-symmetric curved band may sit one grid cell (4.85 points at the test scale) on the other side of its axis than on Windows (see PORTING_BLOCKERS.md, Not reproducible on iOS).
- Superseded / updated 2026-11-20 (job 5): part (b) is parity now. Windows `b9902e6` `takeoff_renderer.py:385-416` `_create_negative_indicator` returns an anchor `QGraphicsPathItem` (no pen) whose children are the red box and the minus (both `ItemIgnoresTransformations`, positioned at the centroid in the anchor's coordinates); `:105-111` sets the item data on the anchor and its children. The page transform of `zoom_handler.py:339-348` (`_get_page_transform`) / `:362-379` (`_apply_page_transform_to_items`, unchanged) is applied to the anchor, so the marker follows the shape on a rotated or flipped page (mechanism read from the code; pinned by the Windows test `test_takeoff_renderer.py:1548-1549` `NegativeIndicatorPageTransformTests.test_the_marker_follows_the_shape_on_rotated_and_flipped_pages`). iOS: no code change; pin added: MarkerAnchor.FollowsTheDisplayedShapeOnEveryRotationAndFlip (test_takeoff_footprint.cpp:805: 7 rotation / flip combinations on a square page and on a non-square one; the invariant pinned is marker == centroid of the displayed outline; on a non-square page Windows pivots the page transform on the unrotated page centre, so absolute Windows scene points for 90 and 270 degrees differ from the iOS-frame points by the constant ((W-H)/2, (H-W)/2), the page-rotation frame difference, not a marker difference). Part (a) (the Qt subtracted-path point order versus the iOS region centroid) is unchanged and stays kept. Status stays fixed.
- Windows defect record ((b) marker on rotated or flipped pages; FIXED on Windows by `b9902e6`, 2026-11-19; was "possible Windows defect", severity cosmetic, confidence medium): at `6d4786f` the negative marker was created with `setPos(centroid)` and `ItemIgnoresTransformations`, and `_apply_page_transform_to_items` then called `setTransform(page transform)` on every takeoff item including the markers, so on a rotated or flipped page the marker was drawn displaced from its shape (`takeoff_renderer.py:105-116`, `:390-417`, `zoom_handler.py:339-348`, `:362-379`). Fixed in `b9902e6` (the marker is an anchor item with child items, `takeoff_renderer.py:385-416`; `zoom_handler.py` unchanged).

- Windows: `cpp_extensions/src/mesh/feature_edges.cpp:109-175; exporters/dxf_exporter.py:32-38`: Edges come from an unordered_set in MSVC STL iteration order, so the LINE order in the DXF is MSVC-specific.
- iOS (as mapped): `Core/Geometry/feature_edges.cpp:109-175; Services/ExportService.mm:153-155`: The same algorithm on libc++, whose unordered_set iteration order differs. LINE order (and which endpoint is first in a LINE) can differ from Windows.
- Windows tests: none found
- note (Phase 1): CAD semantics are order-independent. The DXFWriter itself is byte-identical for the same line list. Verifier: LINE entity order follows unordered_set iteration (feature_edges.cpp:109-175), which is MSVC STL specific and cannot be matched under libc++. ...
- outcome (cannot-reproduce): Not reproducible on iOS: DXF entity order is the iteration order of std::unordered_set of the STL in use (open disposition, nothing to port). Files: `Core/Geometry/feature_edges.cpp:109-173; Services/ExportService.mm:151`.

### Decisions that follow the re-baselined Windows behavior

- **MSH-16** (fixed, export-formats): one rule for every export format and the 3D view: a negative subtracts only from positives of the same condition type, a fully consumed positive is dropped, negatives are never output. One shared Core boolean pass (`Core/Meshing/BooleanPass.*`) called by ExportService.mm and ProjectService.mm; delivered together with RB-01, RB-02, RB-03, EXP-05 and MSH-15 (all fixed).
- **EXP-22** (fixed, export-formats): a negative-only export (or any export where nothing survives the boolean pass) reports "Nothing to Export" in every format (OBJ, DXF, HTML) and writes no file (RB-02); a fully consumed positive is dropped. The wording of the alert was a candidate question (EXP-21); the user kept the iOS wording on 2026-11-19.
- **MSH-19b** (fixed, meshing): iOS already kept the plain wall when the wall and drop-stub union fails; the warning log with the takeoff UID, the empty-face union counted as failure and the catch of a throw (shared with RB-04) are done in `Core/Meshing/MeshFactory.cpp`.

### Cross-references created by the decisions

- **GEO-15** and **EXP-17** (wont-fix for winding / byte-order parity): triangulation sets are fixed by GEO-14 (status fixed; equivalence tests, no ordering/winding change). iOS meshes stay outward-facing.
- **RPV-22** (wont-fix for curved placement and the centre handle): its two remaining obligations are carried by GEO-18 (draw existing curves) and RPV-M03 (a drag must not corrupt the control point); both are fixed.
- **POS-M01**, **DBP-31** and **BRW-16** share one outcome: the bid open fails with an error naming the cause (takeoff UID, missing reference, cycle); no silent drops (all three fixed-ui-unverified: the alert is UIKit).
- **IMP-17** (wont-fix): stored + MSZIP stay; unsupported compression types fail with a clear error (done together with IMP-15 and IMP-M03 in Core/Import/CabExtractor.cpp).

### Decisions of 2026-11-19

On 2026-11-19 the user closed the open blockers (message "Close out the open porting blockers"). The 8 formal items that were `blocked-needs-decision` and the 15 candidate items that sat inside otherwise fixed items were decided: **21 keep-iOS decisions** without a code change (19 items; IMP-20 has three sub-rules, RPV-27 (a) and (b) count as one) and **4 code changes**, each written test-first (COND-STYLE-02 and COND-ELEV-01 deliberately deviate from the literal Windows behaviour, DLG-FINITE-01 only for its Rise / Run half, UND-09 ports Windows). Status rule: the 8 formal items DBP-04 (covers DBP-05), BRW-09, EXP-12, EXP-13, EXP-16, IMP-20, LP-24 and RPV-29 changed from `blocked-needs-decision` to `wont-fix` (kept by user decision 2026-11-19; for IMP-20 the decided DATETIME rule itself is fixed and tested); the candidate items keep their status and the question inside them is marked decided, except COND-STYLE-02 and COND-ELEV-01, which are `fixed-ui-unverified` now because their Obj-C part was then only syntax-checked (the version of 2026-11-19 has since also compiled against the real iOS SDK on CI, 2026-11-20 UTC; job 5 changed it again and that version compiles on CI too (run 44856186199, 2026-11-21 UTC), and so does the version of job 6 (run 44953904172, 2026-11-21 UTC); until job 8 it had not run on a device or simulator; COND-STYLE-02 and COND-ELEV-01 were verified on device on 2026-11-21, job 8: DEV-03, DEV-04 and DEV-10 PASS, and are fixed again). Everything the message did not mention stays as it was. Machine-readable: `header.decisions2026_11_19` and the per-item `decisionUpdate` in `PARITY_DIVERGENCES.json`. Job 5 (2026-11-20) overtook 8 of the 21 keep-iOS decisions and the two deliberate deviations by following the fixed Windows behaviour of `b9902e6`: see the last column of the table and [Job 5 outcome](#job-5-outcome).

<a id="possible-windows-defects-job-6"></a>
#### Possible Windows defects found in job 6 (Windows 49a2d59; nothing was changed on Windows; ported as is or not ported, as stated)

The three changes of `49a2d59` were ported in full; the oddities found on the way are listed here and in the records (`possibleWindowsDefectsJob6` of the three records in `PARITY_DIVERGENCES.json`: 7, 5 and 4 entries).

- **COND-ELEV-01, the foot-mark rule (`edit_condition_dialog.py:72`, `:1437-1461`), 7 findings (ported as is):** (1) one ASCII `"` anywhere in the text switches the whole rule off, so `5'x"`, `5'6x"`, `5'abc"` and `5'x1/2"` are saved as 60 inches, `10'6.3"` as 120 and `6"5'7` as 60 (confirmed by the owner 2026-11-21 (job 7) as a possible Windows defect, ported as is); (2) the class is ASCII-only: `5'<e acute>`, `5'_`, `5'<U+0663>` (Arabic-Indic three), `5'<U+FF16>` (fullwidth six), `5'<U+017F>`, `5'<U+212A>` and CJK after the mark are accepted as 60 inches although something non-blank follows the mark; (3) U+201D and U+2033 (and U+201C, U+2019) do not count as an inch mark: `5'6<U+2033>` is refused, `5'6<U+2033>"` is accepted; (4) the lone-x exemption needs the x to be the last non-blank character of the whole text and is decided for each foot mark (`5'x` accepted, `5'x'` refused, `5'_'x` accepted; U+200B, U+FEFF and U+180E after the x are not white space); (5) `\s*` between the mark and the character is unreachable for a first foot mark (the shared parser refuses a blank there) and `$` is redundant (harmless); (6) pre-existing, not new: the dialog catches only ValueError, so a feet run beyond the float range is an uncaught OverflowError in the Qt slot, iOS refuses it with the normal message (an existing deliberate deviation); (7) a stored name such as "Footing @T 5'6" opens with `5'6` in the Elevation field and EVERY dirty save of that condition is refused until the elevation is fixed or cleared (`_apply_changes` validates only a dirty form, `:1760-1765`; parity, owner-visible, see owner note l). The findings were executed against the real Windows `elevation_text_inches` and the verbatim regex (a probe run while the job was planned, and the 14,900,788-string corpus of the reviewers).
- **COND-M08, 5 differences:** see the COND-M08 record: the quantity reset on every Windows save (NOT ported, decided by the owner 2026-11-21 (job 7); a possible Windows defect: silent data loss, it also hits unknown types; job 6 called it a "wrong-number risk"; confidence high), the unknown item kept after a Save, the Spacing written when a real style is picked, abs(rise) / abs(run) on a notes-only edit, the tower-crane note warnings (not ported).
- **DLG-FINITE-01, the allocator guard, 4 findings (no iOS counterpart for the first three):** (PWD-1, low) `renumber_conditions` raises `ConditionNumberOverflowError` (`condition_operations.py:781`) but its `except Exception` (:802-808) has no dedicated re-raise before it, unlike `duplicate_conditions` (:141-142), `duplicate_conditions_to_bid` (:241-242), `insert_condition` (:344-345) and `update_condition` (:733-734), and re-raises only when `_record_caught_mutation_error` is true (on the Access path a pyodbc.Error inside a transaction only, `mdb_writer.py:216-219`; the SQL-Server writer returns true in every case, `sql/writer.py:1199-1203`, and so re-raises: that path was not checked further): on the Access path the error is logged (:805-807) and `False` is returned, so the handler (`condition_action_handler.py:1357-1365`) shows its generic "Failed to renumber conditions." plus the database-locked hint under "Renumber Conditions" and the new renumber text is never shown; (PWD-2, info) only the local Access path carries `user_message`, the SQL Server queue paths were not checked; (PWD-3, info) the docstring of `ConditionNumberOverflowError` (`update_condition_dto.py:10`) still says "A renumber would shift ..." although it now also covers new numbers; (PWD-4, info, existing) a plain failed Duplicate without a message shows nothing on Windows, iOS keeps its "Duplicate Error" alert (decided by the owner 2026-11-21 (job 7): the title stays, the message text is identical to Windows). Not repaired: files written by an older iOS build may already hold -2147483648 (a wrapped duplicate) or 2147483648 (an update shift); the guard does not repair them (Windows has no repair either) and a stored value above INT_MAX still reads as negative on iOS load (`ProjectStore+Load.cpp`, `column_int`). The Windows real-Access test and the New Condition, paste and copy-to-bid paths were not run (no iOS counterpart at job 6; New Condition has one since M1 (2026-11-24)).

#### Kept, researched, not a defect

Kept iOS behaviours whose Windows side was researched and judged NOT a Windows defect (28 sub-items): deliberate, test-pinned or harmless design choices.

- **DBP-04** (decided 2026-11-19): NULL / missing TakeoffIncrements loads as 1.0 (already ported): Not a defect.
- **BRW-09** (decided 2026-11-19): restore from Deleted Bids with a vanished OrigBidProjectUID fails the whole restore group: Not a defect: a deliberate referential-integrity rule.
- **DBP-33** (decided 2026-11-19): NameFontColor default (iOS writes 0 on insert): Not a defect.
- **EXP-21** (decided 2026-11-19): export error text 'Export function returned False': Not a defect: deliberate and test-pinned wording.
- **EXP-09** (decided 2026-11-19): page order = click order in multi-page exports: Not a defect: a harmless design choice.
- **IMP-20** (decided 2026-11-19): (2) BidTexts.Name and BidCallOuts.Name encoded as latin-1 bytes, raising for characters outside latin-1 (iOS stores UTF-8 text): Not a defect (on the import side): the legacy column is a latin-1 byte blob and Windows deliberately raises instead of silently replacing characters; decoding latin-1 never fails, so an OST/OSP produced by Windows always re-encodes.
- **IMP-20** (decided 2026-11-19): (3) memo and IMAGE (longbinary) text stored as a UTF-8 BLOB (iOS keeps TEXT): Not a defect: deliberate and consistent.
- **COND-FOLDER-01** (decided 2026-11-19): cdn_type_name sentinel 'Unknown' in the loader (iOS keeps ''): Not a defect: 'Unknown' for no type and for a dangling type uid is a deliberate loader convention, mirrored by the entity default and several consumers; the dialog hides it (uid lookup first, so a real type named 'Unknown' still works).
- **COND-ELEV-01** (decided 2026-11-19): is_top / z_value taken from the dialog but memory comes from a reload: Nothing of consequence: the two DTO keys are never persisted and Windows reloads the conditions from the database after every save, so Windows memory always equals what a reload derives from the name.
- **RPV-29** (decided 2026-11-19): Normal flip in the 3D lighting (iOS flips towards the viewer, Windows orients normals to +z): Not a defect on its own: orienting shading normals to +z is deliberate and test-pinned, and the shader lights with the raw normal on purpose.
- **RPV-26** (decided 2026-11-19): Minimum interactive sizes (8 px count item / 2 px linear band at Windows view_scale 3.0; iOS uses 8/3 pt and 2/3 pt): Not a Windows defect: the minimums are fixed pixel constants in scene pixels and are consistent in the renderer and the drag/placement code.
- **RPV-27** (decided 2026-11-19): (a) negative marker anchor of an area with backouts (Qt subtracted-path point order versus iOS region centroid): Not a defect: Windows feeds the points of the Qt-subtracted path (several subpaths concatenated) into one polygon centroid, which is not the area centroid of the visible fill, but the contract (anchor inside the visible fill, with an interior fallback) is test-pinned and met.
- **RPV-16** (decided 2026-11-19): Page switch also clears the selected / place condition and the FAB placement availability on iOS (Windows keeps the sidebar condition highlighted): Not a defect: Windows drops the takeoff selection on a page switch (pinned) and leaves the sidebar condition highlighted; iOS clearing the condition as well is the safe direction.
- **UND-02** (decided 2026-11-19): insert_takeoffs validates every parent against rows that exist BEFORE the batch (iOS accepts a parent restored earlier in the same batch): Not a Windows defect: Windows never restores a takeoff under its original uid (the writer allocates new uids), so a parent has to exist before the insert.
- **GEO-M02** (decided 2026-11-19): drag validity (polygon_is_valid) evaluated on scene coordinates instead of OST coordinates: Not a practical defect: validity is decided on coordinates scaled by OST * 72 * view_scale / scale_ratio, so for exactly collinear or touching (degenerate) polygons the answer can depend on floating-point rounding of that scale factor.
- **EXP-15** (decided 2026-11-16): HTML export includes hidden-layer conditions (iOS filters them): Not a defect: deliberate and test-pinned.
- **EXP-18** (decided 2026-11-16): export page and takeoff order follows the user's selection order (iOS sorts): Not a defect: deliberate and pinned.
- **IMP-17** (decided 2026-11-16): LZX and Quantum cabinet compression (iOS decodes stored and MSZIP only): Not a Windows problem.
- **DBP-34** (decided 2026-11-16): boolean columns: Windows writes the Access Yes/No true value (-1), iOS mixes 1 and -1: Not a Windows defect.
- **DBP-M05** (decided 2026-11-16): per-page selected area (BidPageSettings.BidAreaSelected) and inactive-area colouring: Not a defect: a deliberate Windows feature (areas are surfaced there, not on iOS).
- **COND-EXTRA-01** (decided 2026-11-16): iOS-only Connect, Tolerance, Snap-to-Linear controls (Windows has no UI for those columns): Not a defect: the columns are part of the OST schema and Windows round-trips them untouched (its update writes only changed fields), it just has no UI for them.
- **GEO-15** (decided 2026-11-16): area meshes: Windows inward (negative signed volume), iOS outward: Not a separate defect: inward in-memory winding of the area, linear and count generators is the Windows convention (the OBJ writer's face swap and the Python flip of a cut positive after the boolean are built around it; since `b9902e6` an uncut positive is no longer flipped).
- **MSH-21** (decided 2026-11-16): flat quantized face shading on iOS instead of Windows' 60-degree crease-angle smooth shading: Not a Windows defect: crease-angle smooth shading is the intended Windows look; flat shading on iOS is a deliberate rendering-layer choice (PORTING_LOG 2026-03-23).
- **RPV-22** (decided 2026-11-16): curved linear takeoffs: no curved placement and no centre handle on iOS: Not a Windows defect: Windows supports curved linears (arc band, three handles, 6-value position); iOS scope decision only.
- **CAM-02** (decided 2026-11-16): camera refit on every empty-to-non-empty page selection on iOS; Windows keeps the camera within a bid: Not a Windows defect: the camera is fitted once per bid scene and kept across same-bid scene updates (pinned); the iOS transition refit is a deliberate iOS addition.
- **COND-PLACE-01** (text of 2026-11-19; note 1 closed 2026-11-20, job 5: PORTED like Windows, it was an iOS divergence and not a Windows defect): note 1: placement left running when the Image layer is hidden: Only an edge case: a condition assigned to the Image layer is hidden and unplaceable after the Image layer is hidden, while the placement tool stays armed (neither suspended nor restored).
- **DLG-FINITE-01** (decided 2026-11-19): whitespace-only Rise / Run: Windows rejects, old iOS accepted as 0: Not a defect: Windows rejects whitespace-only Rise and Run with 'Rise must be a number.' / 'Run must be a number.' (an empty field means 0).
- **UND-09** (decided 2026-11-19): 'Count as Negative Quantity' acts on the plan-view selected takeoffs only: Not a defect: Windows changes only the takeoffs passed in (the plan-view selection) and pushes one local history entry; this is the behaviour the iOS code change copies.

#### Questions: 1 open (owner note b, below); the 3 of 2026-11-19 were closed on 2026-11-20 (job 5)

- **DLG-FINITE-01** (condition number above the int range): CLOSED 2026-11-20 (job 5) by Windows. Windows `b9902e6` caps the condition number at the Access Long limit 2147483647: `edit_condition_dialog.py:1464-1492` refuses a number below 1 with "Condition number must be a positive whole number." and one above the limit with "Condition number must be between 1 and 2147483647."; `condition_operations.py:623-641` refuses a renumber whose shift would push another condition past the limit (nothing is written); `update_condition_dto.py:5-9`. iOS follows (range message, `MAX(RefNo)` probe with a full rollback and the Windows text, "Save Failed" alert); the answer to the question below is "keep the int range, with the range message". History (asked 2026-11-19): WINDOWS edit_condition_dialog.py:1449-1469 (6d4786f): int(text) with no upper bound, only a value below 1 refused, so any whole number the column holds is accepted (up to 64 bits). IOS: ConditionFormRules.cpp parse_condition_number refused 2147483648 and up (Condition::ref_no is an int, INT_MAX). ASK was: widen Condition::ref_no and the column reads to 64 bits, or keep refusing 2147483648 and up?
- **COND-PLACE-01** (note 1: Image-layer exemption on hide): CLOSED 2026-11-20 (job 5): PORTED. Windows has the exemption for the single-layer toggle only (`ui_event_coordinator.py:6474-6477` skips `_suspend_active_layer_tool` when the hidden layer is the Image layer, `:6504-6505` skips the restore; Hide All / Show All stay unguarded) and refuses a tap for the then hidden condition (`placement_mode.py:1648`); iOS now does the same for the single toggle and has the companion guard (`ost_data::placement_tap_accepted`: sink, floating button, optional delegate query `planView:canPlaceWithCondition:`). It was an iOS divergence, not a Windows defect. History (asked 2026-11-19, judged an edge case, ASK: copy the exemption?): IOS treated the Image layer like any other layer and left the placement tool.
- **COND-PLACE-01** (note 2: layer-less conditions on Hide All): CLOSED 2026-11-20 (job 5): NO LONGER A DEFECT. Since Windows `b9902e6` Hide All no longer hides layer-less conditions (`project_data_service.py:675-700`, the LP-22 fix), so a placement armed on a layer-less condition stays armed on a visible, placeable condition (never suspended: `ui_event_coordinator.py:1474-1491`, pinned by `test_ui_event_coordinator.py:18908-18912`); iOS matches and pins it (CondPlace01_LayerlessCondition.ALayerlessPlacedConditionIsNeverSuspendedAndStaysVisibleAfterHideAll). - Quantities: Windows math.ceil raising on a non-finite quotient is not reproduced (no throwing from the quantity path); parsers: feet digit runs of 309+ digits (Windows OverflowError) return (0.0,false) on iOS; formatting: Windows quirks ported as is (format_quantity_number prints -0 / -0.00, display_to_mm strips any run of trailing m).
- Export rules: a cut positive whose faces were all removed by remove_degenerate_faces is not counted as surviving (Windows would export an empty file); meshing: the Windows ERROR log of a failed boolean_union is not ported (only the WARNING).
- Plan view: a stored negative or non-finite BidPages Width/Height is treated as missing (612 x 792) where Windows carries it into the transform; a rotation that is not a multiple of 90 draws an unrotated canvas and no takeoffs; image layers named image are decided by smallest sequence then uid.
- Plan view: Windows draws small mid handles on the in-progress area polyline preview; iOS only on the rectangle being dragged (RPV-32 text).
- Services: LP-12 write-back of the saved page on pick is not ported (optional per item); load_project fails a bid with two BidSettings rows like Windows.
- ViewController: undo of a delete selects only the deleted takeoff (iOS has one selected takeoff); pre-existing hazard: a takeoff selected in 3D stays selected after switching to 2D although its page may not be the 2D page.

## (F) Cannot reproduce on iOS

- **EXP-24** (ui-cosmetic): DXF LINE entity order is the std::unordered_set iteration order of the STL in use. Evidence: Windows `cpp_extensions/src/mesh/feature_edges.cpp:109-175; exporters/dxf_exporter.py:32-38`; iOS `Core/Geometry/feature_edges.cpp:109-173` (the `std::unordered_set` is at :124) and `Services/ExportService.mm:151`. CAD semantics are order-independent. The DXFWriter itself is byte-identical for the same line list. Verifier: LINE entity order follows unordered_set iteration (feature_edges.cpp:109-175), which is MSVC STL specific and cannot be matched under libc++. ... Final status: cannot-reproduce (nothing to port).
- Partial: exact Qt/locale ordering of folder names (BRW-M01) and the machine-dependent ANSI code page of legacy CAB member names (IMP-18) cannot be reproduced bit for bit. Both were decisions in section E and are fixed with the closest reproducible rule (BRW-M01: case-insensitive ASCII compare, lowercase first, then UID; IMP-18: cp1252 for names without the UTF-8 flag).

## (H) Windows features with no iOS counterpart (list only)

From the Windows-only inventory (87 features). `[platform-only]` = tied to the Windows platform (not a candidate for iOS). This is the Phase 1 inventory. The rule for the fix phase was core logic equal to Windows, only the platform layer adapted, and NO new features, so none of it was scheduled. A few entries turned out to be parity items that sections A-D already counted and are implemented there; they are marked `[implemented ...]` below. All other entries are unchanged.

### ai-takeoff

- AI takeoff analysis (PDF linework, text and region finding): Read-side AI tools: sheet listing with scale hints, PDF text and vector segment extraction, closed-region finding with door-gap closing and dashed-outline handling, quant ...
- AI takeoff proposals (scale and slab elements): propose_scale, propose_element and polygon simplification that build slab conditions and takeoffs from detected regions, with high-impact assumption tracking (scale, thic ...
- AI changeset review, apply, undo and discard: Review dialog showing outlines, added area/volume and assumptions (Accept disabled until high-impact ones are settled). ...
- AI assumptions sidecar and audit log: Per-bid assumptions saved under ~/.ost_visualizer/ai_takeoff, a rebind prompt when the database moves, and an audit log of tool calls and decisions.
- AI takeoff MCP helper, local pipe bridge and MCP Setup tab [platform-only]: ostv-takeoff-mcp stdio helper exposing 15 tools, talking to the running app over a user-only named pipe with a rotating session key. ...
- Read-only MCP server for databases (ost-visualizer) [platform-only]: ostv-mcp stdio helper exposing about 40 bounded read tools and prompts (projects, bids, pages, conditions, takeoffs, summary, PDF text/vector summaries, scope-gap checks) ...
